author: Justifier925
body:
In general, spell sword has a lot more versatility than cavalry, as it’s both a warrior and mage class. Cavalry is a warrior class, so if you play it like a mage you won’t be as effective.

Additionally, because you’re losing the ability to use mage gear, your armour may also suffer. Cavalry is better if you have good warrior gear, and Druid is better if you have mage gear

author: Cptnwhizbang
body:
Early on in the game, you have three main class paths: Warrior, Mage and Thief. Some tiers (2*, 3*, etc) are hybrids between these class. Spellsword uses Mage and Thief gear for example. Classes you unlock grant all the skills permanently and you can swap classes you've unlocked at any time without cost.

Specializations only give their skills while specced, and cost Orns each time you change. At higher levels spec swapping is very common, but at lower levels you will probably just pick one for the tier and stick with it. 

As far as weapons and elements go - if you are using a weapon that your class/spec combination is proficient with, you deal 5% more damage. Dealing damage of the your own element (Water, Lightning, Fire, Earth) also deals bonus damage, though some monsters resist those elements and it's not worth it against them.

Skills usually deal damage based on your attack stat, and spells usually deal damage based on your magic stat, though a few exceptions exist and state as much. Hybrid classes like spellsword usually have a natural balance on those stats so you can use either/both. If your best weapon is a staff, you'll probably be best off using spells. Likewise, if your best weapon is a sword, you'll have higher attack than magic and therefore skills will deal more. Aim to have the highest stat screen attack or magic you can get, and do your best to match elements to your own when possible.

Lastly, against high defense targets like raids and players, there is a hidden stat for each skill and attack called penetration. The default attack has the highest penetration but deals relatively low damage. Attacks that strike multiple times, like tri-cut, strike multiple times, but have lower penetration. The result of this is that attacks like that deal high damage to soft targets, but get zeroed on players or raids. If you have high enough attack/magic they still hit fine, but often it works best using single strike attacks.
